_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: Sam answered all eleven decisions on the sheet the same night it went over, and this session executed them. The glyph clean-up ran: 115 marks off control labels across 23 files, 16 more off the dashboard generator so the daily run cannot restore them, and the three previously protected marks went too. The sweep now refuses to touch a label the generator regenerates — 13 of the 16 sites in the dashboard HTML were the generator's, and without that guard the clean-up would have quietly undone itself overnight and reported success. Two of his answers closed questions rather than opening work: the Sky reads right at its current speed, which two sessions of headless measurement could not settle because every number was taken on a machine that is not his; and the live-session banner is not broken, it has two switches and only one was flipped. Two items were retired outright. Still open and none of it needs him: the 25 CO-blue-on-white pairs, the legacy-anchor retirement (id-keyed, so it lands as a re-mint), and drawing an emptied discipline, which turns out to be a builder change rather than the one-line tweak it was described as.

items.text: The live-session banner is not broken — it has two switches and you flipped one. The claude.ai visibility toggle decides whether the link WORKS; a row in COBI decides whether the banner SHOWS. That row is still pointing at an earlier session and its four-hour life ran out yesterday evening, so the banner correctly showed nothing. Admin → Live-session banner already says so (“Now: not showing (the link expired)”): paste this session's link, pick a duration, press Show the banner. Setting it is deliberately yours, not the session's — it announces a link anyone on the team can open.

The glyph clean-up ran. 115 marks came off button and link labels across 23 files, and 16 more off the dashboard generator so the daily run cannot put them back — including the three we had previously protected, which you confirmed were in scope. Control-label glyphs went from 516 to 401; what is left needs a reworded sentence rather than a deletion, so it is not mechanical. Worth a look at the Activities cards and the curation buttons to say the labels still read right.

The largest remaining source of dark-mode faults is mechanical: 25 places paint a CO-blue background and then hard-code white text on it, so the pair cannot follow the theme. (An earlier note here said about 140 — that figure was measured with a looser pattern over a wider set of files, and counted every blue background rather than only the ones paired with a literal white.)

Some cards and table cells hard-code a white background, so they stay light islands when the page goes dark. The Workplan Goals cells are the worked example and they are written by the daily generator — so the fix belongs in excel_to_dashboard.py, never in the HTML, which the next cron would overwrite.

The SkyView lane file is two and a half times its size budget and the docs lint says so every run. It is invariants rather than stacked history, so compacting it means reading and ruling on each one — several predate decisions that superseded them. Worth its own sitting rather than another append.

Your ruling on where skill statements come from unblocked the course outline's skills layer — published agency standards are the text of record, an ACE exhibit fills a gap they leave, the MAP team overrides either, and a genuine conflict shows both side by side. But we hold none of that text: of 1,987 credentials classified, 64 of them welding, not one carries a skill field. So this is now a fetching problem, not a decision. The question for you is which published standard to start with — an AWS welding certification is the natural pilot.

You asked for a magic phrase people type before they can move a course, shifting to a team phrase later. That would be the first time anything is written from the map, which today writes nothing at all — so it goes through Governance and the privacy review before it ships rather than after. DR-24 now carries your name as its owner; say the word and the phrase gets scoped.

DR-24 is a governance row with an owner and no surface yet: an added skill lands as proposed with the reviewer's name and the day, and joins the published outline when a second curator agrees; a removal works the same way in reverse. Building that means the map's first write, so it routes through Governance and the privacy review first.

Two housekeeping items behind the CPL face. Fifty-five exhibits in the articulation crosswalk are no longer in today's MAP feed; they stay on the map flagged in words rather than dropped, and the fix is a re-seed of the crosswalk from a fresh custom report. And the credit-funnel numbers the face carries for context were read by hand on 2026-09-07; refresh them after the next custom-report load.
